answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can price each new seat with a bond that scales super-linearly in the number of identities, so one honest wallet holds a single cheap bond while ten hollow clones in the same cluster pay far more than any reward they could split, and each opal-thin clone stake becomes unprofitable. Random per-epoch audits sample bonded accounts, and correlated faults slash the whole cluster, so faking a zenith of influence costs more than it returns.
